GEOMETRY — highest priority. Follow Image 1 exactly.
- Table orientation: the table is turned about 40 degrees to the camera. Its long edges run left to right, rising about 12 degrees toward image right; its short edges recede toward the upper left. The laptop faces the user-facing edge.
- User-facing edge: the table edge nearest the camera, in front of the laptop. In the image it runs from -20% across, 98% down to 120% across, 52% down, about 26% of image height below the laptop's lowest point. No tabletop beyond this edge.
- Product on the table: the laptop is 6.0 cm (about 0.3 laptop depths) from the user-facing edge. The tabletop extends 0.54 m (about 1.7 laptop widths) toward image left of the laptop and 0.74 m (about 2.4 laptop widths) toward image right.
- Table size: 1.60 m x 0.75 m, about 5.1 laptop widths by 3.4 laptop depths.
- Frame crop: 3 of 4 table corners fall outside the frame; keep them cropped and never shrink the product to show them.
- Product: exactly as in Image 1 (details: Image 3), occupying 25-70% across and 30-72% down. Same size; never enlarge or move it.
- Camera: 1.21 m high, looking down 11.3 degrees, about 67 mm lens.
detail.layout: Rectangular studio worktable. Its long edges rise toward image right, and its short edges recede toward the upper left. The near long edge faces the user, crossing diagonally from near the lower-left frame boundary toward the right side. The laptop sits a narrow hand-width from this edge, about a third of its base depth. The top extends roughly one and three-quarter laptop widths to its left and two and a half to its right. Only the far corner toward the upper right remains inside the frame; the other three corners stay cropped. The tabletop stops at the drawn straight boundary.
detail.camera: Use a viewpoint around standing waist height, looking gently downward, with the screen face, keyboard deck and left chassis edge visible. Keep the restrained, slightly compressed perspective and existing close framing. All furniture shares the same horizon and coherent vanishing directions. No camera roll, raised viewpoint or wider view.
detail.scene:
An active illustration and ceramics studio. The worktable has a substantial pale birch rectangular top, a shallow apron and simple gray steel legs, with its back against the reference wall. Beyond the user-facing boundary, show the apron, open knee space and a warm-gray concrete floor. In the near right foreground, a wood-seated studio stool on steel legs is partly tucked beneath that long edge, facing the laptop; only a modest portion appears at the bottom-right crop, smaller than the laptop.

The far wall is warm off-white plaster. Across the upper-left and upper-center wall, a broad dusty-blue woven-fabric reference pinboard provides a conspicuous blue surface, roughly twice the laptop's width, hung at comfortable standing viewing height well above the tabletop. Pinned botanical reference sheets depict leaves and stems only, with indistinct, unreadable annotations; leave generous fabric visible around them. In the far upper-right plane, two shallow wall-mounted wooden shelves hold several closed, unlabelled glaze jars, each much smaller than the laptop screen.

In the middle-left plane, on the tabletop beside the laptop along the user-facing side, place a paper sketchbook open to blank cream pages, its spread approximately one laptop width. Slightly farther back on the left tabletop, loosely overlap a few illustration sheets of ordinary drawing-paper size, showing nonhuman abstract shapes and plant forms, with any markings indistinct and unreadable and no signatures. Keep both groups entirely beside the laptop, not in the narrow strip directly in front of it.

In the middle-right plane, on the tabletop beside the laptop, place a plain off-white brush jar holding a few wooden-handled paintbrushes, immediately beside a shallow white watercolor mixing palette about half a laptop width across. The brushes reach approximately half the height of the open laptop. In the rear-left plane, anchor a small potted leafy plant on the tabletop against the wall, in a plain stoneware pot; its overall height is comparable to the laptop screen, with foliage confined to the clear space on the left. In the rear-right plane, place a compact gray articulated studio task lamp on the tabletop beneath the shelves, its shade directed toward the palette and its arms contained to the right of the laptop. Leave usable space between these supplies and the computer.
detail.look: Broad, soft daylight enters from above and screen-right, with generous ambient fill and gentle shadow transitions. Keep the entire studio readable, with balanced highlights and restrained contrast rather than a dramatic product spotlight. Use neutral daylight color, quiet cream and pale wood tones, subdued gray metal and natural green foliage, without a global blue or orange cast. Show fine wood grain, woven fabric, slightly curled paper corners, faint pigment residue in the palette and subtle worktable wear. The mood is focused, calm and recently used, not pristine or display-like.
